title: Bills of Lading and Transport Documents: Release Against a Letter of Indemnity
content:
Sometimes the originals of a `Bills of Lading and Transport Documents` set cannot be produced at destination. On certain document types the line will then release the cargo against a letter of indemnity instead. This page sets out where that is possible, who signs, the bank guarantee behind the letter, the earliest release date and the fee.

## Clauses

1. **Availability.** Where the originals cannot be presented, the letter-of-indemnity route is open only on a type that offers it.
2. **Signatory.** The letter is given by the consignee, and nobody else can give it. On a type whose signatory is shown as "consignee and bank", the letter must also be backed by a bank guarantee.
3. **Amount of the guarantee.** The bank guarantee equals the declared cargo value on the document multiplied by the type's guarantee percentage and divided by one hundred, rounded to the nearest cent.
4. **Earliest date.** Such a release may be granted no earlier than the type's waiting period after the cargo was discharged at the port of discharge. The earliest permitted date is reached by adding the type's waiting days, as calendar dates, to the discharge date recorded for the container at that port. Release on the earliest permitted date itself is allowed. The recorded discharge date governs, not a date given by the caller.
5. **Fee and record.** A release against a letter of indemnity is charged the type's fee to the consignee, and the release is recorded as having been made on a bank-guarantee-backed letter of indemnity.

## Values by document type

| Document type | Release against letter of indemnity offered | Signatory | Bank guarantee (percent of declared cargo value) | Fee (USD per release) | Earliest release (calendar days after discharge) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AHL Sea Waybill | No | not applicable | 0 | 0.00 | 0 |
| AHL Electronic Bill of Lading | No | not applicable | 0 | 0.00 | 0 |
| AHL Straight Bill of Lading | Yes | consignee | 0 | 150.00 | 1 |
| AHL Negotiable Bill of Lading | Yes | consignee and bank | 200 | 200.00 | 3 |
| AHL Combined Transport Bill of Lading | Yes | consignee and bank | 200 | 200.00 | 3 |
| AHL Switch Bill of Lading | No | not applicable | 0 | 0.00 | 0 |

## Worked example (hypothetical figures)

An `AHL Negotiable Bill of Lading` carries a declared cargo value of 48,250.75 USD. The guarantee is 48,250.75 multiplied by 200 and divided by one hundred, which gives 96,501.50 USD, already a whole number of cents. On an `AHL Straight Bill of Lading` no bank guarantee is called for, the consignee's own signature being sufficient.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical dates)

| Document type | Discharge date recorded | Earliest permitted release | Requested release date | Allowed? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AHL Negotiable Bill of Lading | 12 October | 15 October | 15 October | Yes, on the earliest date |
| AHL Negotiable Bill of Lading | 12 October | 15 October | 14 October | No, one day early |
| AHL Straight Bill of Lading | 30 April | 1 May | 1 May | Yes |

## Basis Q&A

**Can the shipper sign the letter of indemnity for the consignee?** No. Only the consignee can give it.

**Who pays the fee for this kind of release?** The consignee.
